fixes.explanation: Priests and prophets sound official, friend, but Amos doesn't name them here. The verse says the ones being oppressed and crushed are the poor and the needy. Those are the people with little, and they're the ones these women are pressing down.

That's it. "Go to Bethel and transgress; rebel even more at Gilgal!" Those are the LORD's words in verse 4. He adds sacrifices every morning and tithes every three days, and I think that's a startling thing to hear. Verse 5 says what it comes down to: it's what the children of Israel love to do.
The text says the opposite, friend. Right after the leavened bread, the LORD says, "…loudly proclaim your freewill offerings." That's an instruction to be loud, not quiet.
False is right. The LORD tells them to offer leavened bread as a thank offering and to "…loudly proclaim your freewill offerings." So the instruction is to be loud, not quiet.
Priests don't appear anywhere in verses 4 and 5, friend. The LORD says, "For that is what you children of Israel love to do…" The text puts it on what Israel loves, not on the priests.

It's actually True, friend. The LORD says, "I struck you with blight and mildew in your growing gardens and vineyards; the locust devoured your fig and olive trees…" So the fig and olive trees were hit as well as the gardens and vineyards. And the same line follows: "…yet you did not return to Me…"

Moab isn't in this verse, friend. The LORD says, "I sent plagues among you like those of Egypt…" That's the comparison He picks, and in the same verse He killed their young men with the sword. Even then, the verse says, "…yet you did not return to Me…"

Edom isn't in verse 10, friend. The land the LORD names is Egypt: "I sent plagues among you like those of Egypt…" The same verse has the sword and the stench of their camp. It's a heavy verse from start to finish.
Yes. The LORD says, "I filled your nostrils with the stench of your camp…" This is a heavy verse, with the sword and the plagues in it. It still ends the same way: "…yet you did not return to Me…"

Smoke and altars sound like they'd go with all those sacrifices, so I see how that one pulled you. But in verse 10 the LORD says, "I filled your nostrils with the stench of your camp…" The camp is what He names. This is a heavy verse, so take it slowly.

The verse doesn't mention dust or a desert. The LORD says, "I filled your nostrils with the stench of your camp…" That comes right alongside the plagues and the sword. The verse ends with "…yet you did not return to Me…"

Nineveh and Babylon are big names, but verse 11 doesn't use them. The LORD says, "Some of you I overthrew as I overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah…" Then He says, "…you were like a firebrand snatched from a blaze…"
Tyre and Sidon aren't in this verse, friend. The LORD says He overthrew some of them as He overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. He describes them as "…like a firebrand snatched from a blaze…"
